subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A non-reducing disaccharide formed from one molecule of alpha-glucose and one of fructose is:
questions.explain: Sucrose is formed by condensation of glucose and fructose and is non-reducing because its reactive groups are involved in the glycosidic bond.

questions.q: The emulsion test for lipids gives a positive result shown by:
questions.explain: Lipids dissolved in ethanol form a cloudy white emulsion when added to water, as the lipid disperses into droplets.

questions.q: During translation, the bond formed between adjacent amino acids on the ribosome is a:
questions.explain: Amino acids are joined by peptide bonds in a condensation reaction catalysed at the ribosome.

questions.q: The genetic code is universal. This means that:
options: The code is read in overlapping triplets
Each amino acid has only one codon
Every codon codes for a different amino acid
A given codon codes for the same amino acid in almost all organisms
questions.explain: Universality means the same codons specify the same amino acids across nearly all living organisms.

questions.q: What is the function of tRNA during translation?
options: To carry the genetic code from the nucleus to the ribosome
To bring specific amino acids to the ribosome according to its anticodon
To unwind the DNA double helix
questions.explain: Each tRNA carries a specific amino acid and pairs its anticodon with the complementary mRNA codon.

questions.q: What is the role of DNA helicase during replication?
options: Breaking the hydrogen bonds between complementary bases to unwind the double helix
Proofreading newly added bases for errors
Joining adjacent nucleotides with phosphodiester bonds
Adding free nucleotides in a 3' to 5' direction
questions.explain: Helicase breaks the hydrogen bonds between base pairs, separating the two strands of the double helix.

questions.q: The primary structure of a protein refers to:
options: the overall 3D folding stabilised by R-group interactions
the association of multiple polypeptide subunits
the specific sequence of amino acids in the polypeptide
questions.explain: Primary structure is the linear sequence of amino acids determined by the gene, dictating all higher levels of folding.

questions.q: Reverse transcriptase is used in genetic engineering to:
options: Synthesise complementary DNA (cDNA) from an mRNA template
Cut DNA at specific recognition sites
questions.explain: Reverse transcriptase makes single-stranded cDNA from mRNA, a useful intron-free copy of a gene.

questions.q: A transcription factor controls gene expression by:
options: Binding to a specific DNA region (e.g. promoter) to stimulate or inhibit transcription
questions.explain: Transcription factors bind specific DNA sequences and either promote or block the binding of RNA polymerase.

questions.q: In a triglyceride, the bond formed between glycerol and each fatty acid is:
questions.explain: Each fatty acid's carboxyl group condenses with a hydroxyl group of glycerol to form an ester bond, releasing water.

questions.q: ATP is resynthesised from ADP and inorganic phosphate in a reaction that is:
options: a spontaneous exergonic process needing no enzyme
a condensation requiring energy, catalysed by ATP synthase
questions.explain: Phosphorylation of ADP is an endergonic condensation reaction catalysed by ATP synthase, storing energy in the new phosphate bond.

questions.q: In eukaryotes, splicing of pre-mRNA involves:
options: Removal of introns and joining of exons
Addition of a poly-A tail only
Removal of exons and joining of introns
questions.explain: Splicing removes the non-coding introns and joins the exons together to produce mature mRNA.

questions.q: Which feature of the genetic code means each base is part of only one triplet?
questions.explain: In a non-overlapping code each base is read only once, belonging to a single codon.

questions.q: The biuret test detects proteins by producing a purple colour, which results from:
options: the formation of a complex between copper(II) ions and peptide bonds in alkaline conditions
copper ions reducing to copper oxide
the breakdown of peptide bonds by acid
questions.explain: In alkaline solution, copper(II) ions form a violet coordination complex with the nitrogen atoms of peptide bonds.

questions.q: A phospholipid differs from a triglyceride in that a phospholipid has:
options: one fatty acid replaced by a phosphate-containing hydrophilic group
only ester bonds and no hydrophilic region
three fatty acids attached to glycerol
questions.explain: In a phospholipid, one of the three fatty acids of a triglyceride is replaced by a hydrophilic phosphate group, making the molecule amphipathic.

questions.q: After 3 complete cycles of PCR starting from one double-stranded DNA molecule, the number of DNA molecules produced is:
questions.explain: PCR doubles the DNA each cycle, so after 3 cycles there are 2 cubed = 8 molecules.

questions.q: A totipotent stem cell differs from a pluripotent stem cell because it can:
options: Differentiate into any cell type including extra-embryonic (placental) tissue
questions.explain: Totipotent cells can form all cell types of the organism plus extra-embryonic tissues, unlike pluripotent cells.

questions.q: Compared with a saturated fatty acid, an unsaturated fatty acid:
options: contains no carbon-carbon double bonds and is solid at room temperature
has a longer hydrocarbon chain by definition
contains one or more C=C double bonds causing kinks, lowering the melting point
is more hydrophilic due to extra hydroxyl groups
questions.explain: C=C double bonds introduce kinks that prevent close packing of chains, so unsaturated lipids have lower melting points and tend to be liquid.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes RNA from DNA?
options: RNA nucleotides are joined by ester bonds, not phosphodiester bonds
RNA contains thymine instead of uracil
questions.explain: RNA uses the pentose ribose and the base uracil in place of thymine, and is typically single-stranded.

questions.q: In the DNA double helix, the two antiparallel strands are joined by:
options: hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs
questions.explain: Complementary bases (A-T, G-C) pair via hydrogen bonds; phosphodiester bonds instead link nucleotides along each strand.

questions.q: Epigenetic modifications differ from mutations because they:
options: Change the sequence of DNA bases
Affect gene expression without changing the DNA base sequence
questions.explain: Epigenetic changes (e.g. methylation, acetylation) alter gene expression without altering the underlying base sequence.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the genetic code?
questions.explain: The code is non-overlapping, not overlapping; each base is read as part of only one codon.

questions.q: In the formation of a phosphodiester bond between two nucleotides, the bond forms between:
options: the base of one nucleotide and the sugar of the next
the phosphate group of one nucleotide and the deoxyribose of the adjacent nucleotide
questions.explain: A condensation reaction links the phosphate of one nucleotide to the sugar of the next, forming the sugar-phosphate backbone.

questions.q: Hydrogen bonding between water molecules arises because water is:
options: a non-polar molecule with even charge distribution
an ionic compound that dissociates fully
a polar molecule with a partially negative oxygen and partially positive hydrogens
questions.explain: Unequal sharing of electrons makes oxygen slightly negative and hydrogens slightly positive, allowing hydrogen bonds between adjacent water molecules.

questions.q: A substitution mutation in a coding region may have no effect on the polypeptide produced. This is most likely because:
options: The degenerate nature of the code means the new codon may still code for the same amino acid
The mutation occurs in an intron only
questions.explain: Owing to degeneracy, an altered codon can still specify the same amino acid (a synonymous/silent mutation).

questions.q: Oestrogen affects gene expression by:
options: Binding to DNA polymerase to speed up replication
Methylating cytosine bases to silence genes
Binding to a receptor to form a transcription factor complex that switches on target genes
questions.explain: Oestrogen binds its receptor, and the complex acts as a transcription factor that initiates transcription of target genes.

questions.q: A polysaccharide gives a positive iodine test (blue-black) and on complete hydrolysis yields only alpha-glucose, including some from 1,6 bonds. The molecule is most likely:
questions.explain: Amylopectin stains blue-black with iodine and is a branched chain of alpha-glucose with both 1,4 and 1,6 glycosidic bonds.

questions.q: Which type of bond is NOT involved in stabilising the tertiary structure of a globular protein?
questions.explain: Tertiary structure is held by hydrogen, ionic and disulfide bonds plus hydrophobic interactions; phosphodiester bonds link nucleotides, not amino acids.

questions.q: DNA ligase is required in recombinant DNA technology to:
options: Form phosphodiester bonds joining the DNA fragment into the vector
questions.explain: Ligase catalyses phosphodiester bond formation, sealing the inserted DNA into the vector backbone.

questions.q: Phospholipids form bilayers in water because:
options: they are entirely hydrophilic and dissolve fully
both ends of the molecule are hydrophobic
the phosphate head is hydrophilic and the fatty acid tails are hydrophobic
questions.explain: The amphipathic nature, a hydrophilic phosphate head and hydrophobic tails, drives self-assembly into a bilayer with tails facing inward.
